title: Introduce execution verifier smokehook and runtime-failure gate
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary: Adds a lightweight execution-verification smoke hook to the eval-harness that runs generated code snippets from execution-targeted prompt sets inside a constrained sandbox. The goal is to detect regressions that cause runtime failures or semantic breaks (exceptions, wrong exit codes, or deterministic output mismatches for small, executable examples) rather than purely surface-level text metrics. Motivation: Several recent regressions in code-generation workloads were only detectable via execution. Relying solely on token/semantic similarity increased false negatives for obvious runtime regressions. This PR introduces a first-class CI hook that can be attached to prompt cohorts annotated for execution testing and integrated into existing CI gates.

What this change does (high level):
- New module eval_harness/hooks/execution_smoke.py implements: 1) a runner interface that supports Python and NodeJS snippets, 2) per-example execution expectations (exit code, stdout matcher, time budget), 3) a scoring function that converts observed failures into a weighted regression score used by CI gating logic.
- Provides a small sandbox image (tools/sandbox/dockerfile.exec-runner) used by CI for deterministic, isolated runs. Sandbox enforces CPU, memory, ephemeral FS limits and disables network by default.
- Adds a CI job (eval_harness/ci_jobs/execution_smoke.yml) that runs the hook on changed prompt-sets or on-demand when the PR touches exec-tagged examples.
- Example prompt set (examples/prompt_sets/executable_examples.jsonl) demonstrating expected metadata per example: language, run_command, expected_stdout_pattern, timeout_ms.
- Tests (eval_harness/tests/test_execution_smoke.py) covering runner timeouts, pattern matching, sandbox invocation mocking, and scoring thresholds.
- Documentation (docs/eval/hooks.md) describes how to annotate prompt sets, configure timeouts, and interpret gate scores.

Design notes and safety: The sandbox has strict resource caps and explicit opt-in for network. The execution hook only runs examples explicitly marked with "exec": true in the prompt set metadata; arbitrary prompts are not executed. We run examples under a minimal unprivileged user inside a container and mount a transient tmpfs. Timeouts are enforced both at the container level and in Python harness logic to avoid stuck jobs.

Scoring and gate behavior: Each example maps to one of three outcome categories: PASS, SOFT_FAIL (non-deterministic mismatch or flaky runtime), HARD_FAIL (exception, crash, or timeout). Gate calculates a weighted failure rate: HARD_FAIL weight=1.0, SOFT_FAIL weight=0.4. If weighted failure rate > 0.05 for a prompt cohort, CI fails the eval gate. Gate is configurable via job parameters and can be set to warning-only in ephemeral branches.

Rollout plan: Start as optional CI job on main for exec-annotated prompt sets (1 week shadow runs), then flip to a required eval gate for repos with high code-generation traffic based on ENG-2479 signals. We will monitor false positive rate and adjust SOFT_FAIL weights and sample size.

Commit summary: - 8c1a2b: initial exec hook module and runner interface - 3f4d7e: add dockerfile and CI job definition - b6d9aa: add example promptset and basic tests - 1a2bb3: tighten timeouts and sanitize inputs - d4e5f6: add docs and CI parameterization

Files changed (high level): eval_harness/hooks/execution_smoke.py — core logic (~430 LOC), tests — unit cases for semantics (~120 LOC), ci job YAML — integration wiring, docs — guidance for annotating prompt sets, sandbox dockerfile.

Review conversation (high level, condensed):
- Evan McCormick (2025-09-04): "Nice end-to-end design. Two asks: (1) ensure we have an allowlist for language runtimes and avoid enabling arbitrary interpreters, (2) can the runner produce structured telemetry (exit_code, runtime_ms, mem_kb) for downstream dashboards?"
- Maya Patel (author) reply (2025-09-04): "Agree on allowlist; initial implementation supports python3.11 and node16 only; added explicit checks. Added structured telemetry output (json lines) to the runner and tests."
- Sofia Liang (2025-09-05): "Concern about flakiness — will this gate be overly sensitive for non-deterministic outputs?"
- Maya Patel reply (2025-09-05): "We added SOFT_FAIL category and sampling-rate parameter to escalate only on sustained regressions. Also safe default sample size is small (20 examples) to limit noise."
- Ravi Kapoor (2025-09-06): "Security question: make sure container image is rebuilt regularly and signed. Also, add an optional dry-run mode that doesn't run containers in PR comments."
- Maya Patel reply (2025-09-06): "Added CI step to pull signed images and a dry-run flag. Documented recommended image rebuild cadence."
- Evan McCormick (2025-09-07): Approved, "Looks good; tests cover core paths and gate tuning is configurable."

CI Summary: The execution_smoke job runs on a self-hosted runner with the sandbox image. The pipeline runs the hook on 20 sampled examples from exec-tagged prompt-sets. Initial run reported 1 SOFT_FAIL and 0 HARD_FAILs; final CI run after fixes passed. Lint, unit tests, and integration job all passed on re-run. ci_status: pass.

Merge outcome: Merged via squash on 2025-09-08 after all approvals and CI green. Merge method: squash. Release notes: "Add execution-verifier ci hook for executable prompt-sets; enables early detection of runtime regressions in code-generation workloads. Configurable thresholds and sandboxed runner included."

Backward compatibility and next steps: The feature is opt-in via prompt metadata. Next PR will add a Grafana dashboard to visualize execution failure trends and wire up alerts when weighted failure rate exceeds configured thresholds. We will also add additional language runtimes after security review.
